original_question: Determine under what conditions a unique solution exists for the consumer-resource system in which consumers move according to the resource gradient from tau time units in the past, under homogeneous Neumann boundary data and in higher spatial dimensions.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 27 in Section 2.3.1, concerning the time-dependent delayed consumer-resource system (2.24) with homogeneous Neumann boundary data and its extension to higher spatial dimensions.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target problem: it is about existence and uniqueness for the delayed consumer-resource PDE system in which the consumer moves along the gradient of the resource from tau time units in the past, under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, with an explicit follow-up about higher spatial dimensions.
missing_details: The exact PDE system (2.24) is omitted. In the paper's notation, the one-dimensional model is u_t = d22 u_xx - d21 d/dx(u d/dx v_tau) + f(u,v), v_t = d11 v_xx + g(u,v), with v_tau(x,t) = v(x,t-tau).
The paper's notation that u is the consumer density and v is the resource density is left implicit; the review also notes that this reverses the roles of u and v from the cited original reference.
The parameter restrictions are missing: tau > 0, d11 > 0, d22 > 0, and d21 >= 0.

The paper first states the model in one spatial dimension; the higher-dimensional case is posed as the natural extension obtained by replacing second x-derivatives with Laplacians and d/dx(u d/dx v_tau) with div(u grad v_tau).

The bounded-domain setting is implicit. To make the question stand-alone, one should specify a bounded interval in the one-dimensional case and a bounded smooth domain Omega subset of R^n for the higher-dimensional extension.
Homogeneous Neumann boundary data should be written explicitly for both unknowns, namely partial_nu u = partial_nu v = 0 on the boundary.
Because this is a time-dependent delay problem, one needs suitably regular compatible initial/history data consistent with the delayed term; your draft does not mention these data at all.

The review keeps the reaction terms general as growth/decay functions f(u,v) and g(u,v); the question should therefore not be narrowed to a particular Holling functional response unless explicitly stated.
The question is specifically about time-dependent well-posedness, not about steady states, bifurcation, or pattern formation.
Ambient setting: real-valued population densities on a bounded spatial domain over R; algebraic items such as degree restrictions or nilpotency conditions are not relevant to this PDE problem.
refined_question: For the delayed consumer-resource system (2.24) in the paper, where u(x,t) denotes the consumer density and v(x,t) denotes the resource density, tau > 0, d11 > 0, d22 > 0, d21 >= 0, and in one spatial dimension on a bounded interval I one has u_t = d22 u_xx - d21 d/dx(u d/dx v(x,t-tau)) + f(u,v) and v_t = d11 v_xx + g(u,v), determine assumptions on the reaction terms f and g and on suitably regular compatible initial/history data under which the time-dependent problem with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions u_x = v_x = 0 on partial I admits a unique solution. Moreover, does an analogous existence-uniqueness theory hold for the natural higher-dimensional version on a bounded smooth domain Omega subset of R^n, obtained by replacing u_xx and v_xx with Delta u and Delta v and replacing d/dx(u d/dx v(x,t-tau)) with div(u grad v(x,t-tau))?
justification: The draft is a near-paraphrase of Open Problem 27. The surrounding paragraph in Section 2.3.1 introduces the exact delayed consumer-resource model (2.24), specifies that the displayed system is the one-dimensional version, defines the roles of u and v and the signs of the coefficients, and then asks exactly for conditions ensuring a unique solution under homogeneous Neumann boundary data, followed by the higher-dimensional extension. Section 5.1.2 later reiterates that the existence problem for (2.24) is open. The refined question therefore restores the displayed PDE, the coefficient/sign assumptions, the bounded-domain and boundary setting, and the intended higher-dimensional analogue, without broadening to other delay or perception models.
